title: Getting Started with excelcompare
text: excelcompare compares Excel files (.xlsx/.xlsm) cell level. Unlike tools compare tabular data, excelcompare captures every cell worksheet — including titles, footnotes, annotations outside main data table.

title: Getting Started with excelcompare
text: main function compare_xlsx(). takes two file paths returns tibble cell-level differences. row represents one cell differs two files: sheet: worksheet name address: Excel cell address (e.g., “A1”, “B3”) value1 / value2: cell content file 1 file 2 status: "modified" (changed), "added" (file 2), "removed" (file 1)
code: file1 <- system.file("extdata", "example1.xlsx", package = "excelcompare") file2 <- system.file("extdata", "example2.xlsx", package = "excelcompare")  diffs <- compare_xlsx(file1, file2) diffs #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Sheet1" | 2 differences #>  #> A1: Title -> Different Title [modified] #> A4: 2 -> 99 [modified]

title: Getting Started with excelcompare
text: default, values compared exact strings. expect small numeric differences (e.g., rounding), use tolerance parameter: Tolerance-aware comparison automatically handles: Numeric cells stored numbers Text cells look like numbers (including comma-decimal like "10,5") Scientific notation (e.g., "1e-5")
code: # Treat differences up to 0.05 as equal diffs_tol <- compare_xlsx(file1, file2, tolerance = 0.05) diffs_tol #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Sheet1" | 2 differences #>  #> A1: Title -> Different Title [modified] #> A4: 2 -> 99 [modified]

title: Getting Started with excelcompare
text: workflows, empty cells zero-valued cells treated equivalent. Enable na_equals_zero = TRUE:
code: compare_xlsx(file1, file2, na_equals_zero = TRUE) #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Sheet1" | 2 differences #>  #> A1: Title -> Different Title [modified] #> A4: 2 -> 99 [modified]

title: Getting Started with excelcompare
text: Use sheet parameter control sheets compared: can also specify sheets name index:
code: multi1 <- system.file("extdata", "example_multi1.xlsx", package = "excelcompare") multi2 <- system.file("extdata", "example_multi2.xlsx", package = "excelcompare")  # Compare all shared sheets (sheet = NULL) all_diffs <- compare_xlsx(multi1, multi2, sheet = NULL) all_diffs #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Data" | 2 differences #>  #> A3: 2 -> 99 [modified] #> B4: z -> w [modified] #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Summary" | 1 difference #>  #> A2: 6 -> 7 [modified] # By name compare_xlsx(multi1, multi2, sheet = "Data") #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Data" | 2 differences #>  #> A3: 2 -> 99 [modified] #> B4: z -> w [modified]  # Multiple sheets compare_xlsx(multi1, multi2, sheet = c("Data", "Summary")) #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Data" | 2 differences #>  #> A3: 2 -> 99 [modified] #> B4: z -> w [modified] #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Summary" | 1 difference #>  #> A2: 6 -> 7 [modified]

text: Compares two Excel files (.xlsx/.xlsm) cell level, identifying differences content based cell position (row, column). function captures cells worksheet, including titles, footnotes, annotations outside main data table.

title: Compare Two Excel Files Cell by Cell — compare_xlsx
code: compare_xlsx(file1, file2, sheet = 1, tolerance = NULL, na_equals_zero = FALSE)

title: Compare Two Excel Files Cell by Cell — compare_xlsx
text: file1 Path first Excel file (.xlsx .xlsm). file2 Path second Excel file (.xlsx .xlsm). sheet Sheet(s) compare. Can : integer character scalar (compare single sheet) integer character vector (compare multiple sheets) NULL (compare sheets exist files) Defaults 1 (first sheet). tolerance Numeric tolerance value comparison. NULL (default) uses exact string comparison (original behavior). numeric value enables type-aware comparison two numeric values considered equal absolute difference tolerance. Character values look like numbers (including comma-decimal notation like "10,5") automatically parsed. na_equals_zero TRUE, treat pairs one value NA 0 identical. Defaults FALSE.

title: Compare Two Excel Files Cell by Cell — compare_xlsx
text: tibble columns: sheet Name worksheet row Row number cell col Column number cell address Excel cell address (e.g., "A1", "B2") value1 Cell value file1 (NA cell exist) value2 Cell value file2 (NA cell exist) status Type difference: "modified", "added", "removed" Returns empty tibble (columns) files identical.

title: Compare Two Excel Files Cell by Cell — compare_xlsx
code: file1 <- system.file("extdata", "example1.xlsx", package = "excelcompare") file2 <- system.file("extdata", "example2.xlsx", package = "excelcompare")  # Compare two Excel files (exact string comparison) compare_xlsx(file1, file2) #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Sheet1" | 2 differences #>  #> A1: Title -> Different Title [modified] #> A4: 2 -> 99 [modified]  # Compare with numeric tolerance compare_xlsx(file1, file2, tolerance = 0.05) #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Sheet1" | 2 differences #>  #> A1: Title -> Different Title [modified] #> A4: 2 -> 99 [modified]  # Multi-sheet files multi1 <- system.file("extdata", "example_multi1.xlsx", package = "excelcompare") multi2 <- system.file("extdata", "example_multi2.xlsx", package = "excelcompare")  # Compare all shared sheets compare_xlsx(multi1, multi2, sheet = NULL) #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Data" | 2 differences #>  #> A3: 2 -> 99 [modified] #> B4: z -> w [modified] #>  #> ── Excel Comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Sheet: "Summary" | 1 difference #>  #> A2: 6 -> 7 [modified]
